evidence_boundary: Hypotheses are OPEN unless explicitly supported by named current measurements; project-owner Clay-native target is fixed and not reopened.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic organ boundaries should be independent from process boundaries; most cognition-hot deterministic organs can share one address space without losing semantic causality.
hypotheses.counter: Separate services are required for every semantic organ to preserve modularity and reliability.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target traces show shared-core colocation creates unacceptable fault propagation or tail latency while service separation remains within latency budget.

hypotheses.claim: A hybrid physical layout with one cognitive core plus isolated model/effect/tool fault domains will Pareto-dominate per-organ microservices under FRANK workloads.
hypotheses.counter: Either a full monolith or full microservice layout dominates after real recovery and IPC costs are measured.
hypotheses.falsifier: Linux/Android target benchmark shows hybrid worse on correctness, p99, recovery and resource use than an alternative.

hypotheses.claim: JSON should be absent from the hot inter-organ data path; compact typed handles/borrowed buffers can materially reduce reconstruction overhead.
hypotheses.counter: Model inference dominates so completely that typed zero-copy handoffs do not materially affect end-to-end performance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target profiling shows serialization below 1% of latency/energy and no measurable benefit from packed/shared views.

hypotheses.claim: Qwen model runtime should remain a configurable physical fault domain rather than a fixed semantic organ process boundary.
hypotheses.counter: One fixed process topology is necessary for correctness/portability.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cross-platform implementation cannot preserve the same Clay ABI when model placement changes.

hypotheses.claim: Capability/effect authority and bearer secrets must remain physically isolated from the cognitive/model core by default.
hypotheses.counter: Typed Clay firebreaks alone are sufficient inside one process.
hypotheses.falsifier: A formally verified same-process implementation proves equivalent containment/revocation and fault isolation with lower cost across all supported effect paths.

hypotheses.claim: Untrusted generated plugins/tool code should execute in a separate sandbox/fault domain with explicit imported capabilities.
hypotheses.counter: In-process generated code can be safely governed solely by semantic tags.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target adversarial tests demonstrate equivalent containment for in-process materialization with no privileged escape paths.

hypotheses.claim: MOSAIC capsule identity should become the per-operation execution identity connecting UnifiedDB, ClayGraph, GWT, MRSC and effect/re-entry receipts.
hypotheses.counter: Existing CognitiveEpochCapsule plus projection receipts are sufficient and MOSAIC adds redundant metadata.
hypotheses.falsifier: Mutation/replay tests show no additional ambiguity or error detection from semantic/instance/basis/selection/view axis separation.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic equality, contract-instance/provenance identity, basis identity, selection-plan identity and reader-view identity must remain independently comparable.
hypotheses.counter: One canonical content hash can safely serve all identity purposes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Property tests across SET/ORDERED/MULTISET/provenance/view mutations find a single identity function with no false equality/inequality under required semantics.

hypotheses.claim: Effect release should revalidate only effect-relevant MOSAIC domains plus hard global invariants rather than demand a global all-domain epoch match.
hypotheses.counter: Global epoch equality is necessary for safe effects.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial target tests find missed effect-changing dependencies under scoped closure, or global validation has negligible false-reject/cost penalty.

hypotheses.claim: Reader-view identity is an audit/causal witness and cannot itself authorize an effect even when it is perfectly validated.
hypotheses.counter: A verified model-facing projection can serve as execution authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: A formally controlled design proves the view object itself is a revocable issuer-bound capability for all effect paths.

hypotheses.claim: UnifiedDB should be a logical typed query/transaction fabric over specialized physical engines, not initially one physical database.
hypotheses.counter: Physical consolidation is required to realize the latency and consistency benefits of Clay-native unification.
hypotheses.falsifier: Dedicated four-baseline target benchmark shows consolidated storage dominates correctness/recovery/p99/write amplification/common-mode risk.

hypotheses.claim: Authoritative event/effect history should remain append/replay capable while graph/vector/FTS/activation stay derived/rebuildable unless separately justified.
hypotheses.counter: Derived stores should be allowed to become co-authoritative for speed.
hypotheses.falsifier: A target design demonstrates equivalent replay/audit semantics with independently authoritative derived views without inconsistency or recovery penalty.

hypotheses.claim: A unified query planner must carry selection provenance and derivation receipts because record authenticity does not prove candidate-set integrity.
hypotheses.counter: Authenticated source records are sufficient for trustworthy retrieval.
hypotheses.falsifier: Selector/query-plan mutations with fixed authentic records cannot alter consequential candidate sets in target workloads.

hypotheses.claim: Incremental maintenance of declared derived views will outperform repeated full recomputation for sparse FRANK state changes, with adaptive rebuild thresholds.
hypotheses.counter: State is small/read-heavy enough that full rebuild is simpler and faster.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target workload traces show incremental maintenance has worse p95/p99, memory, recovery or integrity than rebuild across the operating envelope.

hypotheses.claim: ClayGraph latent activation should remain pre-workspace salience only and must not be treated as GWT ignition.
hypotheses.counter: Persistent graph activation is sufficient operationally to define workspace ignition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stage-orthogonal interventions establish equivalence of activation and workspace mechanism under matched candidate/projection/re-entry state.

hypotheses.claim: A truthful latent memory field can improve candidate availability without explicit retrieval if shuffled/zero-field controls and exact visible facts are matched.
hypotheses.counter: Any benefit comes from extra information/order rather than latent memory state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target factorial finds no truthful-specific benefit after matched visibility/order/budget or shows shuffled field performs equally.

hypotheses.claim: GWT experiments must independently pin or randomize UnifiedDB plan, ClayGraph activation, candidate set, workspace selection, MRSC rail/view and re-entry.
hypotheses.counter: Whole-pipeline ON/OFF ablations are adequate for causal attribution.
hypotheses.falsifier: A validated causal model shows bundled interventions recover the same direct effects without bias across target experiments.

hypotheses.claim: Re-entry learning/reward updates must bind to the exact prior MOSAIC/Workspace/reader/effect episode.
hypotheses.counter: Outcome association by temporal proximity is sufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target replay shows temporal association yields identical credit assignment and no cross-episode contamination under concurrency.

hypotheses.claim: Full-model Clay adaptation should transcode pretrained capability rather than overwrite it, using source-task rehearsal/distillation and checkpoint-level retained-capability gates.
hypotheses.counter: Pure Clay-only full fine-tuning is sufficient and more efficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched target training shows Clay-only full FT retains baseline capabilities while meeting Clay fluency/semantic-execution goals.

hypotheses.claim: Loss-adaptive learning-rate scheduling is compatible with the owner-required full-model adaptation and can reduce forgetting without freezing the model permanently.
hypotheses.counter: Standard full-FT schedule is equally stable when rehearsal is used.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched Qwen3-4B Clay adaptation shows no retained-capability or convergence benefit from loss-adaptive scheduling.

hypotheses.claim: Tokenizer strategy must be an explicit factorial: current tokenizer vs continued-BPE extension vs aligned vocabulary adaptation, because compact Clay benefit is not guaranteed by syntax alone.
hypotheses.counter: A hand-designed compact Clay vocabulary can be adopted without tokenizer experiments.
hypotheses.falsifier: All tokenizer arms converge to equivalent compression, capability and Clay semantic execution under matched compute.

hypotheses.claim: MRSC P2 discrete-native competence must be trained and evaluated separately from P1 canonical semantics.
hypotheses.counter: Canonical Clay fluency automatically yields optimal compact P2 performance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target model shows direct canonical and compact-native views equivalent across accuracy/OOD/cost without dedicated P2 training.

hypotheses.claim: P3 latent-native communication should remain optional and non-authoritative until hidden-state interfaces and message-content causal tests exist on the target runtime.
hypotheses.counter: Latent communication should become default because published systems show speedups.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target heterogeneous runtime exposes stable latent interfaces and passes truthful/shuffled/zero/foreign-message causal tests with robust gains.

hypotheses.claim: Training evaluation must include semantic execution, role binding, authority-class separation, retained general capability and OOD composition rather than Clay perplexity alone.
hypotheses.counter: Low Clay validation loss is sufficient evidence of successful internalization.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across checkpoints Clay loss perfectly predicts all retained-capability/semantic-execution outcomes with no hidden failures.

hypotheses.claim: Bounded Assemblies are a memory-system requirement on mobile because KV cache grows linearly with context and can rival model-weight memory.
hypotheses.counter: Qwen3-4B native long context can be used routinely on phones without architectural context budgeting.
hypotheses.falsifier: Sustained target Android traces show 32k context fits RAM/thermal/latency budgets with no meaningful benefit from bounded Assembly compilation.

hypotheses.claim: Linux and Android should share Clay semantic/runtime contracts but use different physical lowerings, inference backends and process layouts.
hypotheses.counter: One identical binary/runtime topology is required for parity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cross-platform benchmark shows a single topology meets all performance/security/packaging constraints with no adapter value.

hypotheses.claim: ReaderProfile must include model, quantization, context/KV policy, runtime/backend, platform and rail/view version.
hypotheses.counter: Model checkpoint identity alone sufficiently defines reader behavior.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cross-quant/runtime/context tests show no material output/performance differences after checkpoint is fixed.

hypotheses.claim: Android should dynamically cap context/prefill based on measured memory/thermal state rather than expose maximum native context by default.
hypotheses.counter: Static maximum context is operationally simplest and safe.
hypotheses.falsifier: Sustained device runs show no memory pressure, thermal throttling or latency instability across maximum context use.

hypotheses.claim: The authoritative host kernel should be minimal and deterministic: bootstrap trust root, parser/validator/canonicalizer, epoch/receipt integrity, capability/effect gateway and recovery primitives.
hypotheses.counter: More cognition/runtime logic should live in the trusted kernel to simplify the system.
hypotheses.falsifier: Expanding trusted code demonstrably reduces total security/recovery risk without increasing unverifiable attack surface or common-mode failures.

hypotheses.claim: Model or self-modification may propose architecture changes but cannot mutate owner contract, authority policy or current executable kernel without an external validated promotion path.
hypotheses.counter: A fully Clay-native self-representing FRANK should self-authorize architecture mutations.
hypotheses.falsifier: A formally verified self-modification capability proves safe authority monotonicity, rollback and owner-policy preservation without an external gate.

hypotheses.claim: Observability/replay should consume immutable receipts asynchronously where possible rather than sit synchronously on every hot-path transition.
hypotheses.counter: Synchronous full tracing is necessary for causal science and recovery.
hypotheses.falsifier: Async tracing loses required causal ordering/receipts or materially impairs recovery/experiment reproducibility.

hypotheses.claim: No current FRANK organ may be labeled emergent solely because C7 integrates it more tightly; E-CERT2 remains the promotion gate.
hypotheses.counter: Integrated Clay-native recurrence plus GWT is sufficient evidence of an emergent organ.
hypotheses.falsifier: A scientific consensus standard replaces lesion/rescue/OOD/multiscale causal requirements with a simpler validated criterion and target evidence meets it.
